title: Colonial rule and Influence in Asia
intro: Colonial rule and Influence in Asia

cards.title: 4.1 Colonialism in Southeast Asia
body: Southeast Asia is a region in Asia comprised of Indochina, the Malay Peninsula, and the Malay Archipelago.
The region is bordered on the north by China; on the east by the Pacific Ocean; on the south by the Indian Ocean; and on the west by the Indian Ocean, the Bay of Bengal, Bangladesh

cards.title: 4.2 British colonialism in India
body: Over the course of the 18th century, British power in India had increased while the power of the Mogul rulers had declined.
A trading company, the British East India Company, was given power by the British government to become actively involved in India’s political and military affairs.

cards.title: Europe in Asia
body: **India:** the British East India Company won the Battle of **Plassey (1757)** and gradually took control. After the **Indian Revolt of 1857**, the British Crown ruled India direct

cards.title: 4.3 China under European influence
body: In 1800, after a long period of peace and prosperity, the Qing dynasty of the Manchus was at the height of its power.
In the beginning of the 20th century, however, the Qing dynasty collapsed.

questions.q: After 1857, British India was ruled more directly by the

options.C: Crown / Raj, not only the Company

why: Answer C: Crown / Raj, not only the Company

Textbook p.88: The British government ruled India directly through a British official known as a viceroy (a governor who ruled as a representative of a monarch), who was assisted by a British civil service of about 3,500 officials.

questions.q: Meiji Japan’s aim was mainly to

options.B: Modernise so it would not be colonised — then it became imperial too

why: Answer B: Modernise so it would not be colonised — then it became imperial too
Textbook p.101: Its local industry was mainly destroyed.
